title: spark-gpt Triton-batched Muon Newton-Schulz
summary: spark-gpt replaces cuBLAS's small batched BF16 Newton-Schulz products on GB10 with a fixed-shape Triton alpha*A@B+beta*C kernel using FP32 accumulation. The kernel reaches 51-64 versus 19-34 TFLOP/s, remains bit-identical under the repository's exact test, avoids autotuning so DDP ranks choose the same path, and falls back on unsupported devices or shapes; isolated optimizer-step time drops from 33.2 to 22.0 ms for dense and 132.9 to 72.7 ms for 8x2 MoE. These are one-device, shape-constrained microbenchmarks rather than end-to-end training results.

title: TorchTitan-NPU grouped-matmul Muon Newton-Schulz
summary: TorchTitan-NPU groups same-configuration Newton-Schulz products for expert parameters and FSDP-reconstructed gradients and dispatches them through torch._grouped_mm instead of many small BMM kernels, targeting host-bound execution on Ascend A3. A deterministic DSV3-16B-16E comparison matches the baseline for 100 steps and profiler captures document the intended kernel consolidation. The commit provides no textual end-to-end speed or memory number, so it establishes numerical parity and an NPU execution optimization rather than a quantified training gain.

title: burn-mamba segmented Muon for fused projections
summary: burn-mamba treats fused Mamba projections as logical column segments for Muon instead of orthogonalizing the entire allocation, and routes each declared segment through its own optimizer while preserving the fused forward GEMM. Per-head scalar channels, rank-1/rank-3 tensors, embeddings, heads, and boundary projections remain on AdamW; per-family plans cover plain, virtual-layer, bidirectional, and MIMO variants, with 206 tests passing. This is an operator-routing and correctness implementation, not a matched quality or throughput benchmark.

title: Logical Muon blocks under fused QKV and SwiGLU projections
summary: This study shows that fusing Q/K/V or SwiGLU gate/up projections is not optimizer-neutral: whole-tensor Muon changes the polar geometry and aspect-ratio scaling, moving weights 8.6e-4 relative to separated updates after three steps. Logical row_blocks restore bitwise-identical Muon updates for identical gradients and checkpoint conversion preserves momentum, while a mere 4e-7 gradient difference from GEMM reduction order grows into 1.7e-3 trajectory separation after five Muon steps because the Newton-Schulz staging casts to BF16. The finding is an implementation-level reproducibility result, not a quality or speed comparison.

title: Metis optimizer-visible expert-bank splitting
summary: Metis splits a grouped 72-expert projection into equal optimizer-visible chunks while materializing one concatenated weight for grouped GEMM, so Muon ownership can be distributed instead of leaving one rank on the entire roughly 0.7-second Newton-Schulz critical path. Autograd splits gradients back into the chunks, and differential tests pin outputs, input and weight gradients, and cache cleanup against the original parameter. The option is restricted to grouped execution without activation recomputation, and the commit reports the eliminated serial bottleneck rather than a measured end-to-end speedup or completed training run.

title: RWKV Anki Muon coverage for LoRA
summary: Moving the model's 27,520 rank-four LoRA projection parameters from AdamW to a separate zero-decay Muon group is the only optimizer change in a paired run and improves two held-out metrics by 0.000174 and 0.000184 while leaving training advantage near zero. LoRA stable rank rises 48-67% relative to the untreated run and throughput remains within noise, supporting a regularization-by-coverage interpretation; however, the model has only 558,212 parameters, the evidence is one paired trajectory, and LoRA norms grow 62% without saturating, making longer runs dependent on a weight-decay follow-up.

title: NanoScale Muon stability ablation
summary: A five-seed TinyStories ablation replaces informal noise thresholds with Welch tests, effect sizes, variance-ratio tests, and Holm-Bonferroni correction. Muon's mean-loss advantage over AdamW is not significant at p=0.121 because one AdamW seed fails, but it reaches the target in 53 versus 106 steps with no overlap and has 176 times lower run-to-run variance; the same harness finds QK-norm changes convergence speed and variance without changing mean loss. Results and scripts are committed, but the benchmark is a 40M in-domain model and optimizer tuning breadth is limited.

title: DMuon mixed-precision momentum and resume parity
summary: DMuon now creates every regular and tensor-parallel Muon momentum buffer in the declared optimizer dtype instead of inheriting BF16 gradients, matching the checkpoint restore path. Before the fix, 167 of 172 owner-managed matrices in a two-rank Qwen3.5 run silently switched from BF16 momentum before saving to FP32 after resume and diverged on the next update; afterward, 14 logged steps match an uninterrupted run bit-for-bit across loss and gradient metrics. Step time remains within the measured 5.1-6.1-second range, at the cost of an FP32 momentum copy per owner-managed matrix.

title: ArcherChat Muon scalar-dtype parity
summary: ArcherChat casts Muon momentum, learning rate, decay, and NorMuon beta2 scalars to the working tensor dtype before applying Polar Express, variance normalization, and cautious decay. Python-float arithmetic had seeded roughly 1e-7 differences that momentum amplified to about 5e-4 on non-square matrices after five steps; the corrected implementation reports exact parameter parity with its nanochat oracle across square, tall, wide, and stacked cases. This is a focused optimizer-step equivalence test rather than a training-quality or throughput result.

title: radiance bounded Muon batching for MoE
summary: radiance caps each same-shape Muon stack at 32 tensors so Newton-Schulz transient buffers do not grow with the number of experts and MoE layers. The prior unbounded stack made a 48-expert 1.06B model OOM on its first optimizer step; at a representative 96-tensor shape, an isolated RTX 5090 benchmark reports 1.48 times lower peak memory, while a regression test matches the unchunked numerical update and dense models remain below the cap. The evidence is an implementation-level memory benchmark, not a completed MoE training comparison.

title: TorchTitan-NPU overlapped Muon state transfer
summary: TorchTitan-NPU pipelines optimizer-state H2D and D2H copies through a bounded current/next schedule shared by Muon expert and FSDP paths, retaining synchronization only at checkpoint visibility boundaries. On eight NPUs, a deterministic 100-step 4.187B DeepSeek-V3 test matches baseline loss and gradient norm exactly; a DeepSeek-V4 profile reduces optimizer-step time from 4478.18 to 3772.27 ms and steady full-step time from 13.245 to 12.681 seconds, with stable 46.57-46.59 GiB peaks. The measurements cover one Ascend configuration and optimize state movement rather than Muon's mathematics.

title: radiance batched Muon and norm-gain routing
summary: radiance batches same-shaped matrices along a leading dimension before Newton-Schulz and uses foreach momentum and decay, reducing its measured Muon microstep from 8.2 to 4.4 ms while matching separate-matrix error against an FP64 reference. It also routes two-dimensional loop-specific RMSNorm gain banks to AdamW instead of Muon, where fixed-spectral updates would incorrectly treat the gains as matrices; a 1000-step check is quality-neutral at 1.9581 versus 1.9590. The commit's larger end-to-end speedup also includes independent loss and CUDA-graph fixes, so it cannot be attributed to Muon batching alone.

title: radiance hybrid-Muon embedding learning-rate sweep
summary: After hidden matrices moved from AdamW to Muon, radiance found that the inherited 3e-4 auxiliary learning rate left the tied embedding/readout as the bottleneck. A pinned-batch 400-step TinyStories sweep improves validation loss from 2.9111 at 3e-4 to 2.1051 at 3e-2, and a 1200-step check improves 2.2341 to 1.7984; raising only the embedding rate recovers 0.754 of the full 0.797 gain, versus 0.416 for norms and gates alone. This is a small single-recipe study, and the same commit contains an unrelated sparse-attention feature that is disabled by default.

title: MarinSkyRL MuonH FSDP2 shard-local update
summary: MarinSkyRL applies MuonH hyperball updates directly to local FSDP2 parameter shards, reuses the direction tensor as scratch storage, gathers only rank-two Muon directions in BF16 before Newton-Schulz, and leaves rank-three expert directions local. It makes parameter-storage dtype explicit, retaining FP32 by default for JAX-compatible MuonH while allowing matched BF16 comparisons; distributed tests inspect all-gather payloads and compare sharded updates with dense and JAX-oracle behavior. No end-to-end peak-memory, throughput, or RL-quality benchmark accompanies the change.

title: Megatron-LM TensorParallelMuon SYRK option
summary: Megatron-LM adds an opt-in --muon-use-syrk flag for TensorParallelMuon and TensorParallelAdaptiveMuon, forwarding the Triton symmetric-rank-k Gram kernel to distributed Newton-Schulz while preserving the old default path. A version gate requires emerging-optimizers 0.4.0 or newer and unit tests verify both rejection on old releases and compatibility when the flag is off. The integration supplies no kernel benchmark, numerical-parity result, or full-training measurement, so its practical speedup remains unquantified here.

title: nanoScaling non-abelian grokking study
summary: A self-contained 33-run suite reproduces modular-arithmetic grokking and extends it to composition in the non-abelian dihedral group D48. Muon closes the memorization-to-generalization gap reliably across its tested learning rates, but tuned AdamW also reaches a 1.0x gap, so the study attributes most delay to learning rate rather than a uniquely Muon mechanism; representation analysis ties successful runs to collapse from about 24 effective irreducible representations to 3-11. The code, configurations, summaries, and CSV results are committed, while roughly 1.7 GB of checkpoints and per-step logs are gitignored and many ablation cells are single-seed.

title: fluffy-llm paired Muon/AdamW Portuguese fables run
summary: Three paired 2,000-step runs use identical batches on a 4.44M-parameter model and a 402K-token Portuguese fables corpus. AdamW at 3e-4 reaches validation loss 2.6269, Muon at the same rate under-tunes at 3.1069, and Muon at 1e-3 reaches 2.3579; wall time stays near 261-267 seconds because only 246K hidden-matrix parameters use Newton-Schulz. The result cleanly demonstrates optimizer-specific learning-rate tuning but is a single-seed, three-point, very small-data comparison with local-only checkpoints.

title: optimizer-benchmark modern Muon and u-muP workspace
summary: This modern fork of the EPFL LLM optimizer benchmark adds Muon-family methods alongside roughly 30 recent optimizers, a modular MLA/Gated-DeltaNet/MoE/MTP model stack, and separate Adam-versus-Muon u-muP learning-rate rules. It ships coordinate checks, learning-rate-transfer sweeps, and launchers across width, depth, token budget, expert count, and batch size, making it a useful controlled comparison scaffold. The commit includes experiment directories and logs, but the README does not yet consolidate them into a comparative result table, so it should be treated as research infrastructure rather than evidence that one optimizer wins.

title: tensor_language Muon learning-rate fairness sweep
summary: Four completed 0.01/0.02/0.04 Muon learning-rate triples show that the inherited 0.02 rate is best or statistically tied for the conventional model in every tested cell, with at most 0.0327 nats across each grid versus 0.1634 nats attributed to the query/key cap. The induction diagnostic is more rate-sensitive only at the depth-2 width-128 boundary cell, while the depth-3 width-128 cell is stable, supporting the claim that the cap changes the mechanism rather than merely repairing a bad optimizer rate. Runs, scripts, and result artifacts are committed, but the experiment is architecture-specific and extends an active repository rather than a peer-reviewed optimizer study.

title: Muon grokking five-seed stability audit
summary: A CPU-only replication runs twenty 100K-step trajectories across five seeds and four conditions for the modular-arithmetic grokking recipe, varying both initialization and train/test split. Muon groks at steps 5300-5400 for every seed but is strictly stable for none; freezing the post-grokking update removes every sub-95% evaluation and raises the minimum by 0.196-0.806. The audit also overturns the paper's single-seed AdamW-stability control: four of five seeds regress and three of five high-rate AdamW runs never grok. It is a small depth-one task, but raw trajectories and deterministic-backend pairing directly test the mechanism claims.

title: TorchTitan-NPU compiled Muon Newton-Schulz
summary: TorchTitan-NPU adds an opt-in torch.compile path for Muon's Newton-Schulz block using the AscendC backend, full-graph capture, and dynamic shapes. The change is tested on an Ascend A3 with a trimmed DSV4 model by aligning 100 optimizer steps between eager and compiled modes, and it updates configuration and documentation alongside the implementation. No throughput, compile-time, memory, or full-training measurements are reported, so this establishes NPU compatibility and numerical alignment rather than a speedup claim.

title: microgpt v8 Muon ablation
summary: A CPU microGPT implementation adds Nesterov Muon with five Newton-Schulz steps, spectral update scaling, and auxiliary AdamW for embeddings, heads, and vectors. In an 8M-token ablation on the prior winning stack, Muon alone lowers validation bits per character from 2.255 to 2.016, with learning rates 0.01 and 0.02 tied ahead of 0.04; ReLU-squared helps AdamW but not Muon, while value embeddings and logit softcapping are neutral at this budget. The reported roughly 1.4x sample-efficiency gain is a small CPU experiment without seed uncertainty or a matched wall-clock comparison.

title: loss-basis-adam reproducibility repository
summary: The official artifact for The Loss Does Not See the Basis, but Adam Does releases the optimizer zoo, gauge-equivalent attention twins, spectral-tail sweeps, hyperspectral experiments, random seeds, learning-rate curves, model-selection rules, and raw control conditions. It supports the paper's classification of Muon as gauge-equivariant and its phase diagram for when Muon's equal-rate singular-value schedule preserves low-rank recovery. Most mechanism experiments are small CPU studies, with only the larger attention twins and H100 replication ladder using accelerators, and the repository accompanies a broader optimizer-geometry paper rather than a new Muon implementation.

title: ablm-forge muP-safe Muon LR scaling
summary: ablm-forge prevents a Muon update-rescaling rule from silently breaking muP learning-rate transfer: match_rms_adamw grows approximately with the square root of width, so muP now selects the original Muon rule automatically and rejects an explicit incompatible combination. A step-based coordinate check spans a fourfold width range, finding only about 1.01x RMS spread for the original rule versus 1.66x for RMS matching; the non-muP default remains unchanged. This is a targeted scaling-law correctness test, not an end-to-end loss or throughput comparison.

title: tensor_language width-1152 Muon benchmark
summary: Under matched data order and optimizer-specific learning-rate sweeps on a 12-layer width-1152 model, vanilla Muon lowers held-out cross-entropy by 0.1485 nats versus AdamW, while a slot-plus-group-lasso recipe retains a 0.0850-nat advantage at about 13% higher step time. Follow-up probes find in-loss lasso remains aligned with Muon's slot metric at Spearman 0.88, whereas proximal lasso creates no exact zeros and has near-zero or negative correlation, showing that its apparent free sparsity constraint is non-binding. Raw JSON, checkpoints, and partial seed controls are included, but the main Muon arms remain close to single-seed and architecture-specific.

title: microlab hybrid Muon checkpoint migration
summary: After microlab split hybrid AdamW parameters into decay and no-decay groups, this change restores older Muon/AdamW checkpoints by migrating moment and step state according to parameter identity instead of the obsolete one-group layout. It also distinguishes genuinely corrupt files from structurally incompatible checkpoint versions, and a real optimizer-step regression test verifies that resumed training updates parameters. This is a backward-compatibility and correctness fix rather than evidence of better optimizer quality, and it reports no training-loss or throughput comparison.

title: microlab hybrid Muon decay routing
summary: microlab fixes two silent hybrid-optimizer routing errors: configured weight decay now reaches Muon instead of leaving roughly 92% of parameters at the class default, while AdamW separates decayed embedding and head matrices from no-decay one-dimensional norm gains and biases. Focused tests pin parameter grouping and effective decay. The same review also hardens compile and checkpoint behavior, but this commit supplies no optimizer-quality A/B and the planned 1B Muon run is not yet complete.

title: PaddleFleet MQA sparse-gate Muon slicing
summary: PaddleFleet fixes operator-aware Muon routing for MQA's block-sparse gate: sparse_gate_proj.weight mirrors the head-major layout of gate_proj.weight and now receives the same per-head orthogonalization specification instead of falling through to a generic full-matrix update. Regression tests verify that plain MLA emits no extra spec and that a two-head sparse gate is split into two hidden-by-head-dimension matrices. The change is a correctness fix with no convergence or throughput benchmark.

title: goai banded Muon parameter loop
summary: goai parallelizes Muon's outer parameter loop while keeping the caller-owned gradient callback serial, overlapping per-parameter Newton-Schulz work and repeated fork/join stalls. On a twelve-core step-only benchmark with two matrices, latency falls from 78.79 to 51.92 ms, or 34.1%; a three-parameter, both-dtype digest including the transpose branch is bit-identical, and race plus mutation checks catch overlapping or dropped bands. The result is CPU- and workload-specific rather than an end-to-end training benchmark.

title: Teleport-Muon gauge intervention round 2
summary: A gauge-fixed Teleport-Muon intervention moves convolution and batch-normalization weights along equivalent-function orbits and transports gradients plus Muon momentum before seven optimizer steps. Across 20 paired airbench seeds, each move raises Muon-spendable first-order descent potential by about 1.20-1.32x, yet final validation and TTA accuracy fall by 0.43±0.13 and 0.39±0.08 percentage points. Code, 41 raw runs, analysis, and finite-difference checks are included; the negative result is confined to one short vision recipe, uses development seeds, and leaves hot-phase-only teleportation untested.

title: Sentinel native CUDA hybrid Muon
summary: Sentinel adds a native C++/CUDA hybrid Muon path for hidden matrices with Adam on embeddings, norms, biases, and the head, plus fused QKV and gate-up momentum, device-side Frobenius normalization, checkpointed optimizer state, and overlap with auxiliary Adam updates. On an RTX 5070 Ti, its fixed-pack 97M-model probe reaches about 11.2k tokens/s versus Adam's 12.5k under the same selective-checkpoint setting. Evidence is a one-shot synthetic throughput probe on one Windows GPU, with no matched convergence result.

title: BiBo rank-one AttnRes optimizer routing
summary: BiBo tests whether rank-one Attention-Residual pseudo-query weights should be treated as Muon matrices. On one 137M-active/657M-total run, routing eleven such vectors to low-rate AdamW improves step-1000 held-out bpb to 0.569 versus 0.579-0.582 for the Muon arms, about seven times the measured noise floor; high-rate AdamW instead ties Muon. The result supports giving rank-one operators a much smaller group-specific step, not an AdamW-geometry claim: it is single-seed, lacks the 2000-step final evaluation, and omits the decisive low-step Muon arm.

title: DeepFin Aurora polar-convergence telemetry
summary: DeepFin adds per-shape-class Aurora polar-convergence telemetry—minimum-to-maximum singular-value ratio and normalized orthogonality error—on the actual update, alongside the configured Polar Express iteration count. Float64 SVD diagnostics reproduce eight cells from a real checkpoint fixture and show why a power estimate missed singular modes more than six orders below the maximum; the change measures under-convergence without altering optimizer numerics. Evidence is one application's checkpoint and telemetry path, not a training-quality A/B.

title: verl-Muon agentic RL reference implementation
summary: The official artifact for the agentic-RL study packages its hybrid MuonWithAdamW optimizer, named-parameter routing, FSDP1 integration, paper-aligned ALFWorld and WebShop launchers, aggregation scripts, and reproduction notes. It warns that the reference NO_SHARD path replicates actor parameters and that the 3e-5 Muon recipe applies 3.53x AdamW's hidden-matrix update RMS, so neither the sharding choice nor learning rate is a universal default; the repository reproduces the paper rather than adding independent benchmark evidence.

title: Sign compression for Muon: SignMuon, MuonSign, and the Limits of Error Feedback
summary: This official reproducibility artifact covers centralized, federated, synthetic-counterexample, and NanoGPT experiments for six sign-around-Muon and error-feedback variants. On a single unseeded 2,330-step 8×H100 run, Muon reaches 3.2785 validation loss, EF21-SignMuon 3.2860, and SignMuon 3.2881; all methods measure 61.41–62.06 ms per step. The artifact includes raw logs and exact reproduction commands, but uses one run per method, two optimizer-code builds, and a slower pure-PyTorch port.

title: Evaluating the Muon Optimizer: From Symbolic Recovery in Signomial Models to High-Dimensional LLM Adaptation
summary: This thesis artifact checks in code, results, trajectories, and figures for 1,160 symbolic-regression runs, 200 classification runs, and a Llama-3-8B LoRA spectral check. Muon records 38 recovery-rate wins versus 9 for AdamW, but is a median 0.70 seconds slower and has 0.59 worse log10 MSE; the staged ECSEL baseline remains faster and more accurate. Classification uses one untuned shared protocol, excludes LOAN, and the LoRA arm is only a confirmatory two-run comparison.

title: KohakUwULLM MuonW
summary: KohakUwULLM adds a native hybrid MuonW path with explicit matrix-versus-AdamW parameter routing, shape-batched Newton-Schulz, cubic and quintic schedules, 3D expert batching, spectral or RMS update scaling, and optional stochastic writeback for low-precision weights. The implementation is substantial, but the commit supplies no controlled training or throughput benchmark.

title: HOT-Step-CPP batched Muon Newton-Schulz
summary: HOT-Step-CPP groups 448 same-shape Muon matrices into Newton-Schulz buckets, reducing one measured optimizer step from 298.6 ms unbatched to 136.1 ms at bucket 8 and 138.0 ms at bucket 16; buckets 64 and 128 regress because chained concatenation becomes quadratic. The author estimates the workload's end-to-end advantage over AdamW rises from 1.02× to about 1.23×, but evidence is one LoKR music-model workload and the remaining 55 ms floor is estimated.

title: NVIDIA Emerging Optimizers per-head Muon
summary: NVIDIA's official notebook demonstrates two ways to orthogonalize attention projections independently per head: reshaping only the momentum update inside the orthogonalizer, or temporarily grouping parameters and state as 3D tensors. Four updates match independently optimized stock-Muon heads with a maximum absolute difference of zero; this is an equivalence example rather than a convergence or speed benchmark.

title: verl native Megatron TensorParallelMuon
summary: verl exposes Megatron-Core TensorParallelMuon, routes matrices to Muon and other parameters to AdamW, integrates layer-wise master-weight buffers, and adds a beta-derived RMS-matching switch. On Qwen3-30B-A3B across 16 GPUs, peak optimizer memory falls 18.3% and actor-update time drops from 15.30 to 7.50 seconds; reward and end-to-end timing remain within run-to-run spread. The evidence is two short 30-step runs, and the measured run used a miscalibrated 0.4227 scale rather than the recommended derived setting.

title: PaddleFleet declarative Muon slicing
summary: PaddleFleet moves Muon slicing knowledge into Transformer modules through declarative slice specifications, covering per-head or separate fused QKV updates, MLA and VHA projections, CSA compressors, fused gate-up FFNs, and grouped 3D MoE experts. The change reports no intended precision change but provides no controlled training or throughput result.

title: Megatron LayerWise Muon expert-gradient counting
summary: Megatron-LM propagates regular and expert tensor-parallel groups into LayerWise Muon's child optimizers so expert biases are deduplicated over ETP rather than the global TP group. A TP2-EP2-ETP1 regression test catches the previous factor-of-two gradient-norm undercount; only expert biases are affected, the practical norm error is expected to be small, and no functional training benchmark is supplied.

title: PaddleFormers Muon Adam-fallback hyperparameters
summary: PaddleFormers now forwards configured adam_beta1, adam_beta2, and adam_epsilon values to Muon's Adam fallback for nonmatrix parameters instead of silently using defaults. The matrix-valued Muon path is unchanged; the fix matters for reproducibility when hybrid parameter groups use nondefault Adam settings.

title: XTuner padded all-to-all for Muon remainders
summary: XTuner adds an opt-in padded all-to-all path when a Muon matrix remainder is smaller than the distributed world size, reducing peak communication memory compared with its default all-gather/reduce-scatter route. The tradeoff is dummy Newton-Schulz work on padding, so the existing path remains the default and no end-to-end throughput result is reported.

title: Modalities native PyTorch Muon component
summary: Modalities adds a configuration and factory component around torch.optim.Muon, exposing Muon and Adam-fallback hyperparameters with construction tests. It delegates the algorithm to PyTorch rather than providing a new implementation and reports no convergence or performance benchmark.

title: RWKV Anki batched Muon Newton-Schulz
summary: An RWKV training campaign groups Muon matrices by shape and batches Newton-Schulz, reducing 2655 matrix multiplications to 75 and measuring an isolated 1.053× clean-card wall-clock gain above a 1.8% noise floor. Combined with torch.compile and fewer data-fetch workers, full training is 1.27× faster with changes 6-8× below cross-seed accuracy spread, so the full gain is not attributable to Muon alone.

title: VeOmni head- and group-wise Muon orthogonalization
summary: VeOmni preserves the logical attention-head or expert-group layout of fused weights, orthogonalizes each block independently, and supports per-block learning-rate scaling instead of reshaping every matrix into one generic 2D view. The change targets tall MLA and grouped projections; its tests cover slicing and updates, while comments warn that splitting near-square or wide QKV matrices can hurt and no training curve is supplied.

title: MindFormers Muon P2P buffer-lifetime reduction
summary: MindFormers writes Muon momentum back earlier and removes a persistent point-to-point communication cache so temporary buffers die sooner without changing numerical results. Across six eight-device Ascend 910B2 configurations, reported maximum allocated memory falls by 972-1533 MiB with neutral or slightly improved step time.

title: yxTPU operator-aware distributed Muon study
summary: This JAX/TPU MaxText fork combines per-head QKV orthogonalization with data-axis-sharded Newton-Schulz and runs six 200-step, 337M-parameter experiments on TPU v4-64. Compensated per-head QKV improves loss by 0.101 nats over its baseline while scale-only splitting is 0.029 nats worse; the authors explicitly treat the short horizon as preliminary and call for a billion-token A/B.

title: goai bit-identical CPU Muon kernel rewrite
summary: The Go neural-network runtime rewrites Muon's latency-bound scalar Gram multiplication into a transposed ikj/AXPY form and exploits symmetry, cutting a step-only benchmark from 418.3 to 200.0 ms, or 2.09×, at the cost of 6% more bytes per operation. Frozen-reference plus zero and infinity fixtures verify bit identity.

title: MaxText DeepSeek-V4 operator-aware Muon
summary: MaxText adds DeepSeek-V4-specific Muon mappings and exclusions for mHC, MLA, and MoE operators, with an automatic ten-step Newton-Schulz schedule of eight aggressive quintic steps followed by two convergent cubic steps. Unit tests and a decreasing-loss smoke run validate the path, but the commit provides no controlled comparison against the standard five-step recipe.

title: VeOmni owner-based FSDP2 Muon all-to-all
summary: VeOmni assigns each full matrix to one owner rank, gathers its shards with paired all-to-all collectives, performs Newton-Schulz once, and returns the update, with buckets and uneven-tail handling for FSDP2. Tests cover parity and communication edge cases, but the commit reports no end-to-end throughput.

title: Megatron-Bridge DeepSeek-V4 Flash Muon recipe
summary: NVIDIA's DeepSeek-V4 Flash recipe runs distributed Muon on 64 GB200 GPUs with beta 0.95 Nesterov momentum, unit-RMS scaling, five quintic Newton-Schulz steps, and an additional 0.2 update scale. A 1000-step convergence run validates the configuration, but there is no matched AdamW or alternate-Muon comparison.

title: TransformerEngine cuSOLVERMp Muon communicator initialization
summary: TransformerEngine lazily initializes the ProcessGroupNCCL communicator, rank, and world size when a cuSOLVERMp Newton-Schulz context first performs a collective, fixing distributed Muon failures when the process group was not previously touched. A regression test covers the initialization path; this is a correctness fix rather than an algorithmic change.

title: EleutherAI Muon metasmoothness run-length grid
summary: EleutherAI extends its optimizer diagnostics with single-seed Muon runs from 250 to 2000 steps, where the reported metasmoothness score changes only from 0.9965 to 0.9947. The authors warn that saturation and missing local-directional-smoothness measurements prevent a robust conclusion, making this a diagnostic baseline rather than evidence of optimizer superiority.

title: NVIDIA Emerging Optimizers Muon without Triton
summary: Emerging Optimizers makes its Triton symmetric-rank-k backend optional and falls back to the regular Newton-Schulz implementation when Triton is unavailable. Regression coverage verifies that Muon remains usable in non-Triton environments; the fallback improves portability rather than convergence or speed.

title: OpenXLA Layered-FSDP Muon collective-broadcast lowering
summary: OpenXLA can lower dynamic-slice collective broadcasts used by Layered-FSDP Muon from 32 full all-gathers to 32 single-layer broadcasts in its HLO test. The optimization is behind xla_spmd_enable_dynamic_slice_collective_broadcast, which defaults to false, and the commit reports compiler-level evidence rather than end-to-end training throughput.

title: Paddle batched Muon byte cap
summary: Paddle adds muon_max_group_bytes to split same-shape batched Newton-Schulz groups according to FP32 momentum-buffer size, bounding temporary memory and avoiding out-of-memory failures. Two-GPU tests preserve numerical behavior; smaller groups can reduce batching efficiency, and no throughput curve is reported.

title: NSL 500M Muon versus AdamW confirmation
summary: A controlled 505M-parameter NSL pretraining run finds the small-scale Muon recipe 2.38 nats behind AdamW at the shared micro-400 point and about 15× slower per micro-batch under optimizer-state offload. The author limits the verdict to this untuned single-seed configuration and calls for a scale-specific learning-rate sweep, resident momentum, and amortized Newton-Schulz.

title: NSL batched TF32 Newton-Schulz and resident momentum
summary: After profiling identified staging and offload as the main 500M bottleneck, NSL adds opt-in shape-grouped TF32 batched Newton-Schulz and device-resident Muon momentum. On 168 matrices with five steps, the batched path falls from 795 to 341 ms and collapses about 2520 GEMM launches to roughly 110 calls, with deterministic and differential gates.

title: ByteDance VeOmni Gram/Quack Muon backends
summary: ByteDance Seed's training framework adds standard, pure-PyTorch Gram, and Hopper+ Gram/Quack Newton-Schulz backends for Muon, with restart controls, hardware fallback, tests, and DeepSeek-V4/Qwen3-MoE recipes; it also clarifies learning-rate inheritance and zero-communication expert sharding.

title: Paddle Muon backward/communication overlap
